caption: A fleece jacket is pulled off over a cotton shirt in the dark, and tiny sparks crackle where the fabrics separate.

sa.check: A person wears a fleece jacket over a cotton shirt, in the dark.
Tiny sparks flash where the fabrics separate.
The sparks come as the fabrics part, not while the jacket is still.

pc.expect: The sparks appear only along the line where the fleece is parting from the shirt and each is gone at once; nothing glows before the jacket moves or after it is off.
pc.fail: The fabric glows steadily like a lamp; or sparks keep flashing after the jacket has been laid still; or a spark stays lit at one spot; or sparks appear on parts of the jacket far from where it is parting.

pc.expect: One jacket and one shirt; the sparks leave nothing behind on either.
pc.fail: Glowing dots stay on the shirt or jacket after the flash; or a second jacket appears; or the jacket vanishes; or the sparks detach and float about the room.

pc.expect: Both garments are soft cloth: the fleece stretches and folds as it comes off and the shirt stays on the body.
pc.fail: The jacket stays a rigid shape as it lifts; or stretches out like elastic and snaps back; or the shirt comes off with the jacket as one piece; or the fabric flows like liquid.

pc.expect: The sparks are small: they brighten only the fabric right around them and not the room.
pc.fail: The room lights up with each spark as if a lamp came on; or the sparks throw shadows across the walls; or the sparks stay lit and light the room.

pc.expect: One person with the same body throughout; the jacket comes off over the body, not through it.
pc.fail: The jacket passes through the body or arms; or the body changes shape; or the jacket merges with the shirt; or an arm detaches with the sleeve.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The jacket's colour, the shirt's colour and the room stay the same apart from the sparks.
pc.fail: The jacket changes colour; or the shirt changes colour; or the room's contents rearrange.

note: The person is kept because the fabrics on the body are the physics; their movements are not judged. The crackle is sound and is not judged.
